RSSI: received signal strength (dBm). Values closer to 0 are stronger.
TX/RX: link transmit/receive rate (Mbps). Some ROMs may report -1.
Retry/s: retransmissions per second, calculated from txRetries. Higher values usually indicate interference or congestion.
Bad/s: bad packets per second, calculated from txBad. Higher values indicate a less stable link.
Quality score: weighted from RSSI, rate, retries, bad packets, and band. For engineering reference only.
Requires root. OPPO-family phones only. Power usage may increase.
2) Works only on some OPPO/OnePlus/realme systems. Other devices may fail or report errors.
3) Low latency is useful for games and may slightly increase power usage.
4) High performance includes low latency and is suitable for large transfers, with much higher power usage.
5) Once enabled, it remains active after closing the app unless you turn it off or reboot the phone.

Current system data network type and NR mode. NSA = non-standalone, SA = standalone.
Radio technology of the current serving cell, such as NR / LTE / WCDMA.
Current band frequency. TDD uses one time-shared frequency; FDD uses paired uplink/downlink frequencies.
System-estimated cellular uplink/downlink capacity. It is not real-time traffic or a speed test result. Tap the row to switch between Mbps and MB/s.
Tracking Area Code, used to identify the area covered by a base station.
Physical Cell ID, used to distinguish same-frequency cells.
NR cell identity, composed from gNB ID and Cell ID.
Absolute radio-frequency channel number. It is usually the center frequency, though some phones report the start frequency.
Band and frequency point. TDD uses one time-shared frequency; FDD uses paired uplink/downlink frequencies.
NR downlink bandwidth: total configured bandwidth / currently active bandwidth, usually fully active only during speed tests.
NR carrier aggregation information, showing each carrier band and bandwidth in MHz. Inactive bands are orange; carriers active on uplink or downlink are blue.
LTE carrier aggregation information, showing secondary-carrier frequency and signal parameters to identify whether 4G CA is active.
Received total energy. Use as a rough reference, mainly available on 4G.
Reference signal power, used to judge coverage strength.
Reference signal quality, useful for cell quality and congestion.
Signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio, useful for estimating practical throughput potential.
